name: Lao

allophone_rules.notes: Lao permits only /p t k m n ŋ w j/ in the coda, and every coronal obstruent letter neutralises there to an unreleased [t̚]: ⟨ລົດ⟩ is /lot̚/ and ⟨ວັດ⟩ /ʋat̚/, not *[lod]/*[ʋad]. Enfield (2007), A Grammar of Lao. Gated on syllable_position=coda so onset /d/ is untouched (⟨ດີ⟩ stays /diː/).
Labial coda neutralisation, the labial half of the same rule: ⟨ຮັບ⟩ is /hap̚/. Enfield (2007), A Grammar of Lao. Coda-gated, so onset /b/ is untouched.
Velar coda neutralisation, the velar half of the same rule: ⟨ດອກ⟩ is /dɔːk̚/. Enfield (2007), A Grammar of Lao.
⟨ຍ⟩ is the palatal nasal /ɲ/ in the onset but the glide /j/ in the coda, the only position a Lao syllable admits it: ⟨ຂ້ອຍ⟩ is /kʰɔːj/. Enfield (2007), A Grammar of Lao.

Lao /ʋ/ is a labiodental approximant in the onset and the glide [w] in the coda, where the labiodental articulation is not available: ⟨ລາວ⟩ is /laːw/ against onset ⟨ວັດ⟩ /ʋat̚/. Enfield (2007), A Grammar of Lao.

⟨ອ⟩ has two jobs. After an onset consonant it is the vowel letter /ɔː/ (⟨ດອກ⟩ /dɔːk̚/); when it opens a syllable of its own it is the zero-consonant carrier that a vowel sign needs to attach to, and is read as the glottal onset (⟨ອິດ⟩ /ʔit̚/). The following vowel is what distinguishes the two, so the rule is gated on the grapheme AND on a following vowel. Enfield (2007), A Grammar of Lao.

notes:
Lao, the Southwestern Tai language of Laos, written in its own Indic-derived abugida. The spec describes the Vientiane standard.

Vowels are written with signs that stand before, above, below or after their consonant, and several are circumfixes. The preposed signs are ⟨ເ ແ ໂ ໃ ໄ⟩: they precede the consonant on the page and follow it in speech, so ⟨ເກ⟩ is /keː/. A circumfix pairs one of them with a post-consonantal part, which is what the multi-character vowel keys ⟨ືອ ຶອ ົາ ົວ າະ⟩ encode: ⟨ເສືອ⟩ 'tiger' is /sɯːə/, ⟨ເຮົາ⟩ 'we' is /haw/, ⟨ເກາະ⟩ 'island' is /kɔʔ/. ⟨ະ⟩ writes short /a/ in an open syllable and carries the glottal check Lao gives such syllables; ⟨ັ⟩ and ⟨ົ⟩ write short /a/ and /o/ in a closed one.

A Lao syllable may close only on /p t k m n ŋ w j/. Every other consonant letter neutralises in the coda, which the LO_CODA_* rules encode: coronal obstruents to unreleased [t̚], labials to [p̚], velars to [k̚], and ⟨ຍ⟩ from onset /ɲ/ to the glide /j/. The rules are gated on the coda, so the onset readings are untouched — ⟨ດີ⟩ is /diː/ while ⟨ລົດ⟩ is /lot̚/. Lao likewise admits no liquid coda, but the fact is left unencoded, and a measurement of the 2308-word kaikki gold says why. Nine words end in ⟨ລ⟩ or ⟨ຣ⟩. Six of the nine have the letter as the ONSET of a final syllable whose vowel is a preposed sign (⟨ກິໂລ⟩ /kiʔ.loː/, ⟨ທະເລ⟩ /tʰa.leː/, ⟨ກຳໄລ⟩ /kam.laj/) or is the subscript of a word-final ho-nam ⟨ຫຼ⟩ (⟨ໄຫລ⟩ /laj/), so a positional rule that fires word-finally reads an onset as a coda in two productive spelling classes and breaks ⟨ໄຫລ⟩, which is currently correct. The remaining three are not one phenomenon and none of them is a liquid the engine could simply neutralise. ⟨ນຄຣ⟩ and ⟨ທຫາຣ⟩ are abbreviated etymological Indic spellings of ⟨ນະຄອນ⟩ /naʔ.kʰɔːn/ and ⟨ທະຫານ⟩ /tʰaʔ.haːn/ — both fully spelled forms are in the same gold and this spec already reads both correctly — so reading them needs the unwritten ⟨ະ⟩ and ⟨ອ⟩ supplied, which no rule about the final letter provides. ⟨ອີແມລ⟩ is the English loan 'email' whose final /l/ is nativised to /n/, a loan-adaptation fact about one word. Three words spread over two unrelated causes do not establish a coda rule, and the rule they would motivate costs more spellings than it fixes.

⟨ຫ⟩ before a sonorant is not an /h/ but the ho nam tone-class marker: the sonorant is the onset and the ⟨ຫ⟩ only shifts the syllable into the high class, so ⟨ຫລອດ⟩ is /lɔːt̚/ and ⟨ຫມາ⟩ /maː/. ⟨ໝ⟩ and ⟨ໜ⟩ are single-codepoint ligatures of the same device, and ⟨ຫຼ⟩ writes it with the subscript lo ⟨ຼ⟩. Before a vowel ⟨ຫ⟩ is a real /h/ (⟨ຫໍ⟩ /hɔː/), which is why the marker is encoded as digraphs rather than as a silencing of ⟨ຫ⟩.

⟨ວ⟩ is the labiodental approximant /ʋ/ in the onset and the glide /w/ in the coda. ⟨ຣ⟩ is read /l/, the ho-nam digraph ⟨ຫຣ⟩ with it: the historical /r/ has merged with /l/ in the modern language. ⟨ອ⟩ is the vowel /ɔː/ after an onset and the zero-consonant carrier /ʔ/ when it opens a syllable itself.

A consonant letter with no vowel sign on it carries the inherent vowel /o/, the value it takes in the closed syllables such a spelling writes (⟨ຄນ⟩ /kʰon/).

Lao has no lexical word stress — prominence is carried by the tone system — so no `stress` block is encoded (research-tier exemption). Tone itself is not written into the IPA: it is a property of the syllable computed from the consonant class and the tone marks ⟨່ ້ ໊ ໋⟩, which are recorded in `tone_inventory` and mapped to nothing segmentally. The circumfixes whose post-consonantal part is ambiguous on its own — ⟨ເ◌ັ⟩ /e/, ⟨ແ◌ັ⟩ /ɛ/, ⟨ເ◌ີ⟩ /ɤː/ — are NOT encoded, because the vowel key cannot see which preposed sign it belongs to; encoding them by position would be fitting the benchmark rather than describing the orthography. Neither is the cancellation mark ⟨໌⟩, which silences the letter it stands on (⟨ວຽງຈັນທນ໌⟩ /ʋiːəŋtɕan/): it is mapped to nothing itself, but the letter it kills is still read.

Three known gaps. The ho-nam digraph ⟨ຫຼ⟩ (ho + subscript lo) does not form word-finally with no following vowel to attach a preposed sign to: ⟨ອາໂຫຼ⟩ reads as ʔaːhoːl (bare ⟨ຫ⟩ /h/ + the preposed ⟨ໂ⟩ + a stray coda /l/ off the subscript) rather than the ho-nam reading ʔaːloː the digraph gives it elsewhere (⟨ໂຫຼດ⟩ /loːt̚/ is correct). The tokenizer attaches a word-final preposed vowel to the single grapheme before it rather than to the longest digraph match, and this spec has not found a clean per-grapheme fix; tracked as a known gap rather than encoded around. Separately, ⟨ເ...ອ⟩ is a preposed-sign/⟨ອ⟩ circumfix like ⟨ເ◌ີ⟩ above and is likewise NOT encoded for the same reason: ⟨ເສອ⟩ reads sɔː, dropping the preposed /eː/ that the circumfix as a whole gives (⟨ໂອເຊອານີ⟩ 'Oceania' loses its second syllable's nucleus). A third gap: bare ⟨◌ວ◌⟩ — ⟨ວ⟩ between two other consonant letters with no vowel sign anywhere in the word — is itself the nucleus /uːə/, not the onset /ʋ/ this spec gives it elsewhere (⟨ພວກ⟩ is /pʰuːə̯k̚/, ⟨ຫຼວງ⟩ /luːə̯ŋ/, 12/12 kaikki gold words with no vowel sign at all agree; dropping that condition and only requiring the C-⟨ວ⟩-C letters widens the set to 36/40, the 4 exceptions all carrying a preposed vowel sign elsewhere in the word that makes ⟨ວ⟩ that vowel's own onset or coda instead, e.g. ⟨ແຫວນ⟩ /ʋɛːn/). Encoding it needs a positional condition joint on both neighbours being consonants, which the grapheme table's single-position lookup cannot express; tracked here rather than encoded around.

kaikki.measured: Lao tone is a property of the syllable computed from consonant class and the tone marks, which this spec records in tone_inventory but maps to nothing segmentally because Lao tone is suprasegmental and not itself an IPA segment the orthography commits to a single reading of. The three named remaining gaps (word-final ho-nam digraph attachment, the e-...-o circumfix, bare intervocalic w as nucleus) are each independently documented as structural tokenizer/lookup limitations rather than unsourced rules, and are not encoded around.
